observation: Read all2198 characters. Risk context leads directly to one specified replacement option, unlike q33's explicit three-option choice. The design contract is ten-to-twenty small dams with total management capacity matched to the current dam; this range is a design constraint, not a reported optimized count. The abstract derives single-dam flow/capacity/cost inputs, differentiates single-dam risk and power from series-level safety, combines the three submodels through AHP, and assigns number/placement to a genetic search before solving heights. It then points to emergency-flow/Lake-protection tradeoffs and ends by announcing sensitivity and strengths/weaknesses. No final count, cost benefit or sensitivity result is reported here. Retain the model hierarchy and dependent outputs; avoid translating a promised analysis into evidence of success. Multiple form-field blocks and five discretionary word breaks still fragment the candidate, so it remains source-unverified. Figure mention is retained as prose only; no diagram, formula or model-correctness verification.
